name: Calvin Cycle
notes: For a genome to encode the Calvin Cycle, it must encode at least 50% of the genes encoding the pathway, plus encode the large and small subunits of 2-Oxoglutarate Ferredoxin Oxidoreductase

name: Reductive Citric Acid Cycle
notes: For a genome to encode the Reductive Citric Acid Cycle, it must encode the defining carbon-fixing reaction (ATP citrate lyase or citryl-CoA lyase), the ferredoxin-dependent 2-oxoglutarate oxidoreductase, and coverage of at least 4 of the 6 remaining core cycle steps

name: Hydroxypropionate-Hydroxybutyrate Cycle
notes: For a genome to encode the Hydroxypropionate-Hydroxybutyrate,it must encode at least 50% of the genes encoding the pathway

name: Dicarboxylate Hydroxybutyrate Cycle
notes: For a genome to encode the Dicarboxylate Hydroxybutyrate,it must encode at least 50% of the genes encoding the pathway

name: 3-Hydroxypropionate Cycle
notes: For a genome to encode the 3-Hydroxypropionate Cycle,it must encode at least 50% of the genes encoding the pathway

name: Wood-Lungdahl Pathway
notes: For a genome to encode the Wood-Lungdahl Pathway,this rule requires evidence for a formate or CO2 reduction entry point, a functional glycine cleavage system, formate-tetrahydrofolate ligase and cyclohydrolase, and either a complete corrinoid/methyltransferase-acetyl-CoA synthase branch or an alternative serine hydroxymethyltransferase route

name: Reductive Glycine Pathway
notes: For a genome to encode the Reductive Glycine Pathway, it must encode a formate dehydrogenase complex, the majority of the glycine cleavage system, it must encode formate-tetrahydrofolate ligase, and methylenetetrahydrofolate dehydrogenase NADP+ / methenyltetrahydrofolate cyclohydrolase, and one of the two pathways of glycine synthesis

name: Syringate

name: 4-Hydroxybenzoate

name: 4-Methoxybenzoate
notes: Presence of 4-methoxybenzoate monooxygenase O-demethylating, which indicates ability to convert 4-methoxybenzoate to 4-hydroxybenzoate

name: Ferulic Acid
notes: Presence of at least one of: FCS;feruloyl-CoA synthetase,  feruloyl-CoA hydratase/lyase; this indicates an ability to utilize ferulate

name: Coumarate
notes: Presence of sam5;flavonoid hydroxylase, which indicates ability to use coumarate

name: Caffeic Acid
notes: Presence of at least two of the CarABCDE genes hydrocaffeyl-CoA:caffeate CoA transferase, caffeyl-CoA synthetase, caffeyl-CoA reductase, electron flavoproteins A and B; this indicates ability to use caffeic acid

name: Gallic Acid
notes: Presence of at least two of the subunits of gallate decarboxylase, indicating ability to use gallic acid/gallate

name: Protocatechuic Acid
notes: Presence of at least one of the chains alpha, beta of the protocatechuate 4,5-dioxygenase or presence of at least one the subunits alpha,beta of protocatechuate 3,4-dioxygenase. This indicates ability to use protocatechuic acid/protocatechuate

name: Catechol
notes: Presence of catechol dioxygenase or catechol 2,3-dioxygenase , either indicating an ability to use catechol

name: Flavones
notes: Presence of at least two of the following: flavone/flaonol reductase, flavanone/flavanonol-cleaving reductase, chalcone isomerase, phloretin hydrolase. this demonstrates ability to break down a flavone compound.

name: Methanol
notes: For a genome to have methanol oxidation capability, it should encode at least one subunit of methanol dehydrogenase

name: Alcohol/Ethanol
notes: For a genome to have alcohol/ethanol oxidation capability, it should encode pyruvate decarboxylase, an alcohol dehydrogenase, an aldehyde dehydrogenase, and acetyl-CoA synthetase

name: Pyruvate
notes: Pyruvate conversion to acetyl-CoA occurs via one of three enzyme complexes: pyruvate dehydrogenase K00163, 2-oxoacid ferredoxin oxidoreductase K00174, or formate-acetyltransferase K00656. Presence of any indicates potential for acetyl-CoA formation.

name: Acetate
notes: Acetate production can occur via the phosphate acetyltransferase‚Äìacetate kinase route K00625 & K00925 or alternative ligase K01905 or hydrolase K01067 pathways. Either route yields acetate from acetyl-CoA.

name: Lactate
notes: Lactate formation can occur through L-lactate dehydrogenases K00016, K00101 or D-lactate variants K03778, K03777. Presence of any indicates capacity for pyruvate reduction to lactate.

name: Butyrate
notes: Butyrate formation proceeds via phosphate butyryltransferase K00634 coupled with either butyrate kinase K00929 or medium-chain acyl-CoA synthetase K01896. Both steps are required for full conversion.

name: Propionate
notes: Propionate formation requires both propionate kinase K19697 and propionate CoA-transferase K01026 for CoA-dependent conversion of intermediates to propionate.

name: Formate
notes: For a genome to have formate oxidation capability, it should encode formyl-CoA acetyltransferase

name: Glucose
notes: Presence of glucose metabolism indicates microbial potential to degrade, transform, or utilize glucose

name: Sucrose
notes: Presence of sucrose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to degrade, transform, or utilize sucrose, a common plant-derived sugar that can fuel rhizosphere microbial activity.

name: Mannose
notes: Presence of mannose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize mannose-containing carbohydrates, supporting turnover of plant- and microbial-derived sugar compounds.

name: Galactose
notes: Presence of galactose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize galactose derived from plant polysaccharides, glycoproteins, or other organic matter inputs.

name: Fucose
notes: Presence of fucose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize fucose-containing sugars, supporting transformation of plant-, microbial-, or mucilage-derived carbon compounds.

name: Xylose
notes: Presence of xylose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize xylose, a major hemicellulose-derived sugar, linking plant polymer breakdown to downstream carbon metabolism.

name: Fructose
notes: Presence of fructose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize fructose and related plant-derived sugars that can support rhizosphere microbial growth and carbon turnover.

name: Arabinose
notes: Presence of arabinose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize arabinose, a common component of hemicellulose and pectin-derived plant carbohydrates.

name: Ribose
notes: Presence of ribose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize ribose, a pentose sugar derived from nucleic acid turnover, linking nucleotide degradation and microbial carbon recycling in the rhizosphere.

name: Rhamnose
notes: Presence of rhamnose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize rhamnose-containing plant or microbial polysaccharides, supporting turnover of complex sugar inputs.

name: Maltose
notes: Presence of maltose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize maltose, a disaccharide released during starch degradation, supporting microbial turnover of plant storage carbohydrates.

name: Trehalose
notes: Presence of trehalose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize or synthesize trehalose, a stress-protective disaccharide found in microbial and plant tissues, linking carbon storage and osmotic stress responses to broader soil carbon cycling.

name: Alkanes
notes: Presence of any aerobic alkane degradation genes per HMMs from CANT-HYD

name: Benzene/Toluene/Ethylbenzene/Xylene
notes: Presence of any BTEX Benzene, Toluene, Ethylbenzene, Xylene degradation genes per HMMs from CANT-HYD

name: Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons
notes: Presence of any PAH polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon degradation genes per HMMs from CANT-HYD

notes: Presence of both a functional reaction core built from specific photosystem proteins and the ability to biosynthesize photosynthetic pigments from at least 2 of 9 key enzymes in the chlorophyll/bacteriochlorophyll synthesis pathway.

name: Hydrogenases
notes: Presence of any hydrogenase

name: Nitrogen Fixation
notes: Presence of any nitrogenase genes, indicating ability to fix nitrogen

name: Aerobic Ammonium Oxidation
notes: Aerobic ammonium oxidation converts ammonia to nitrite through sequential reactions catalyzed by ammonia monooxygenase and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase. Presence of one ammonia monooxygenase subunit set and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase indicates this capability.

name: Aerobic nitrite oxidation
notes: Presence of nitrite oxidoreductase, indicating ability to oxidize nitrite

name: Anaerobic Ammonia Oxidation ANAMMOX
notes: The genome is an anammox if it encodes the genes required to oxidize ammonium to dinitrogen gas

name: Dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium DNRA
notes: DNRA reduces nitrate to ammonium through a two-step process: nitrate reduction via Nar or Nap systems, followed by nitrite reduction via Nrf or Nir enzymes. Presence of one nitrate reductase system and one nitrite reductase system indicates DNRA capability.

name: Nitrate reduction to Nitrite
notes: Nitrate reduction to nitrite can occur through either the membrane-bound Nar system (K00370, K00371) or the periplasmic Nap system (K02567, K02568). Either system completes the nitrate transformation step.

name: Nitrite reduction to Nitric Oxide
notes: Nitrite reduction to nitric oxide (NO) is carried out by either NirS (K00368) or NirK (K15864). Presence of either gene indicates capacity for nitrate/nitrite reduction in denitrification.

name: Nitric Oxide reduction to Nitrous Oxide
notes: The conversion of nitric oxide (NO) to nitrous oxide (N‚ÇÇO) is catalyzed by nitric oxide reductase, encoded by norB (K04561) in bacteria or CYP55 (K15877) in fungi. Presence of either gene indicates the capacity to perform this denitrification step

name: Nitrous Oxide reduction to Dinitrogen gas
notes: The reduction of nitrous oxide (N‚ÇÇO) to dinitrogen gas (N‚ÇÇ) is catalyzed by nitrous oxide reductase (nosZ, K00376). Presence of this gene indicates the potential for the final step of denitrification, converting greenhouse gas N‚ÇÇO into inert atmospheric N‚ÇÇ.
